definitions.explanation: The day of the year with the longest period of daylight, occurring around June 21 in the Northern Hemisphere.

examples.japanese: {夏至|げし}は{六月|ろくがつ}にある。
examples.english: The summer solstice is in June.

examples.japanese: {夏至|げし}の{日|ひ}は{一年|いちねん}で{一番|いちばん}{昼|ひる}が{長|なが}い。
examples.english: The summer solstice has the longest daytime of the year.

examples.japanese: {夏至|げし}を{過|す}ぎると{少|すこ}しずつ{日|ひ}が{短|みじか}くなっていく。
examples.english: After the summer solstice, the days gradually get shorter.

notes:
The summer solstice, one of the 24 solar terms ({二十四節気|にじゅうしせっき}) in the traditional East Asian calendar. It falls around June 21 each year.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {夏至|げし}の{日|ひ} — the day of the summer solstice
- {夏至|げし}を{迎|むか}える — to reach the summer solstice
- {夏至|げし}を{過|す}ぎる — to pass the summer solstice

RELATED TERMS:
- {冬至|とうじ} — winter solstice (opposite season)
- {春分|しゅんぶん} — vernal equinox
- {秋分|しゅうぶん} — autumnal equinox

CULTURAL NOTE:
Unlike the winter solstice, which has strong food traditions ({冬至|とうじ} pumpkin, {柚子湯|ゆずゆ}), the summer solstice has fewer widespread customs in Japan, though some regions celebrate with specific local foods.
